scenario.name: PyTorch Official Security Advisory, Sonatype & MITRE T1195.001 — PyTorch torchtriton Nightly Dependency Confusion Supply Chain Attack & h4ck.cfd DNS Exfiltration
scenario.overview: Imagine a research workshop whose nightly supply clerk checks a public downtown parts market before checking the company private warehouse whenever an internal part name is ordered. An opportunist rents a booth in the downtown market under that exact internal part name with a shiny higher version tag, tricking the clerk into carrying a disguised spy box straight onto high-powered research benches where it packs up local keys and whispers them out disguised as tiny postal-lookup cards. In this scenario (T1195.001, PyTorch Official Security Advisory, Sonatype & MITRE T1195.001, PyTorch torchtriton Nightly Dependency Confusion Supply Chain Attack & h4ck.cfd DNS Exfiltration), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: public PyPI Namespace Squatting, then __init__.py Execution of Compiled ELF, then aES-Encrypted DNS Tunneling Exfiltration. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Public PyPI Namespace Squatting, then __init__.py Execution of Compiled ELF, then AES-Encrypted DNS Tunneling Exfiltration, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on Auditd Event 59 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Public PyPI Namespace Squatting & `pip --extra-index-url` Precedence Hijack
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1195.001 - Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools)
stages.description: Noticing that a famous lab nightly toolkit relies on an internal helper name not yet reserved on the public marketplace, the attacker claims that exact name on the public shelf so the automated buyer prefers the public fake over the lab private bin. PyTorch nightly Linux packages depended on an internal package named torchtriton hosted on https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cu117. Because users ran pip3 install --pre torch --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/..., and pip evaluates BOTH public pypi.org and the extra index and picks whichever has the highest version number, the attacker uploaded a malicious torchtriton wheel with a higher version to public pypi.org (logged in Linux Auditd Event 59 with VulnerabilityClass=Dependency Confusion , --extra-index-url precedence flaw, HijackedPackage=torchtriton , PyTorch Nightly Linux Dependency, MitreId=T1195.001 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
